I am an old woman, sixty-three years, and I never went to school. This small maize plot is near the house, and I plant it like my mother showed me — with cowpea and a little pepper between the maize. I have no money to waste on big bags of fertilizer for this small piece; last year I put the goat and chicken droppings from my compound, and the maize was enough for the house. I will do the same this year, with my own seed I kept from last harvest, and my grandchildren will help me weed.
